notes: Tests followup jumpy temperature trace. Corrected after the Wave 1 agent source review: questions and rubrics distinguish procedure scope, supported alternatives and missing deployment inputs. Claims: t-table-erratic-01, t-table-inaccurate-causes-01. These fixture-wide anchors are provisional retrieval labels unless a turn supplies explicit evidence; they are not human sign-off. The current direct-feed slice contains four probe datasheets, so its coverage does not establish the manual-specific requirements.

turns.content: The water temperature on one of our pods has gone jumpy - it steps around by a degree or two between readings while everything else on the same instrument looks steady. Where do we start looking?

must_contain: points at the connections at the meter and at the sensor, either loose or dirty, as a first thing to check
points at a break somewhere in the cable
Distinguishes the erratic-reading checks from dirty-sensor and expired-verification causes of inaccurate readings, noting weak batteries can cause either.
must_not: attributes the jumpiness to real changes in the water without checking the instrument first
invents a numeric tolerance or drift specification for the temperature sensor
jumps straight to replacing the sonde

turns.content: If it turns out to be the cable, can we just swap it ourselves and carry on?

must_contain: warns that swapping the cable is not necessarily a free repair, because changing cables can require the sensor to be recertified
Attributes the conditional NWIS uncertainty rule to the temperature chapter, rather than asserting current platform capability; requires re-verification after repair.
Requires verified accuracy before treating repaired-sensor data as verified; checks whether cable replacement invalidates certification and requires recertification.
must_not: says a cable swap is a simple field fix with no follow-up
invents a recertification interval, cost, or provider
confuses recertification of the sensor with a routine calibration of the other sensors
